newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -Dlr/mark slowly but surely eyes new highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Dlr/mark slowly but surely eyes new highs.

text.p: Dollar/mark, having drawn strength from doubts about the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), is heading for a test of 1.7530 resistance and a fresh 40-month high, analysts said.
Dollar/mark surged to 1.7465 on Monday, its highest since the week ended on February 20, 1994.

"The whole EMU concern helped dollar/mark pop up to new highs, but it has been running into good selling interest at the top," said David Solin, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analystics. "It's topping out. But it's possible, feasible to see 1.7530 in another attempt at the top side."
Chartist Ben Morden at I.D.E.A. said the intermediate resistance for dollar/mark is 1.7465, the retest of the high on Monday, followed by a major hurdle in the 1.7520/30 area.
The 1.7520 level is where the upper end of a rising channel from April comes in, while 1.7530 was the next high in 1994 -- also set in the week ended on February 20.
Dollar/mark had established a 1994 peak a few days earlier, on February 8, at 1.7686 -- likely a tough level to take out, analysts said.
"Closing today above 1.7423, the prior 1994 high set on June 6, would be very constructive," Morden predicted.
At 1930 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.7450/55 versus 1.7438/43 at the open and at 114.62/67 vs. 114.33/43.
Morden said dollar/yen, still lackluster, was continuing to somewhat decouple from dollar/mark.
"Some more mark/yen buying would help dollar/yen. There is strong support at 65.50/55, for a run at 65.80 to 66.10," Morden said as mark/yen changed hands at 65.68/70.

Foreign Exchange Analytics's Solin expected dollar/yen to improve in the more quiet environment that followed the post-G7 summit tension highlighted by a call by Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto for foreign exchange cooperation.
"Dollar/yen can probably go higher, as high as 117.00," Solin said, referring to the 38-percent retracement of the fall from 127.47, the May 1 high, to 110.62, the June 11 low.
Solin noted 117.00 yen also is the recent high on May 28.
"The market is starting to sense dollar/yen is more stable," said Solin who agreed with Morden mark/yen may "go higher," maybe to 68.00 and help dollar/yen in the process.
However, before attacking 117.00, dollar/yen must convincingly take out a falling resistance trendline that is coming at 115.55/60, chartists said.
